summary: recce/services/kafka.py implements a minimal ApiVersions handshake + MetadataRequest v1 probe. It parses brokers and topic names and emits two findings (kafka_metadata_leaked, kafka_saslgated). Beyond that it uses none of the ~70 other API keys in the Kafka wire protocol: it cannot enumerate SASL mechanisms, cannot attempt auth with looted creds, cannot read data, cannot list consumer groups, cannot describe configs/ACLs, and cannot fingerprint the broker version. It also throws away fields already sitting in the response it parses (controller_id, rack, is_internal, ApiVersions body) and never speaks TLS despite listing 9093/9094 as target ports. Multiple facts it does capture (advertised broker hosts, ports, rack IDs) are never fed to other services.
existing_capabilities: ApiVersions v0 handshake (KIP-511 warmup) — response is discarded
MetadataRequest v1 — parses broker node_id/host/port and topic names
kcat-based runbook stubs (metadata + consume) — cred-free only, no credentialed variant

missing_capabilities.name: SaslHandshakeRequest (ApiKey=17) enumeration
missing_capabilities.description: Never sent. SaslHandshake v0/v1 returns the enabled_mechanisms array (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256/512, GSSAPI, OAUTHBEARER, PLAIN-SASL_INHERIT). This is the single most useful pre-auth fact against a SASL-gated broker: it dictates which mechanism a spray campaign must use, and OAUTHBEARER/GSSAPI vs PLAIN implies very different downstream infrastructure (Keycloak/Kerberos KDC). KIP-43 / Kafka protocol guide §SaslHandshake.

missing_capabilities.name: SaslAuthenticate (ApiKey=36) with looted creds
missing_capabilities.description: analyze() ignores the creds argument entirely. There is no credentialed path — SASL PLAIN / SCRAM-SHA-256 / SCRAM-SHA-512 auth attempts are never made even when other services have looted a user/pass. Given that Kafka commonly reuses LDAP / DB / SMTP passwords, this leaves the highest-value primitive on the table.

missing_capabilities.name: Fetch (ApiKey=1) — bounded data sample from open topics
missing_capabilities.description: When metadata leaks freely, ANONYMOUS is very often also permitted READ on user topics. Module never issues a Fetch, so it cannot prove data disclosure. A bounded 1-record-per-topic fetch from earliest offset would upgrade kafka_metadata_leaked from HIGH inventory-leak to CRITICAL data-disclosure with sample payloads.

missing_capabilities.name: ListOffsets (ApiKey=2) — activity + volume signal
missing_capabilities.description: Never sent. earliest+latest offsets per partition disclose per-topic message counts and staleness, letting the operator prioritize which of dozens of leaked topic names actually contains fresh data before running Fetch.

missing_capabilities.name: ListGroups (ApiKey=16) + DescribeGroups (ApiKey=15)
missing_capabilities.description: Consumer group IDs are named after the consuming application (e.g. `fraud-scorer-v2`, `keycloak-audit-sink`). DescribeGroups additionally returns members with their client_host, group_instance_id, and client_id — attacker-observable inventory of downstream services and the hosts running them. Currently unqueried.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Kafka protocol ListGroupsRequest v0-v4, DescribeGroupsRequest v0-v5

missing_capabilities.name: DescribeConfigs (ApiKey=32) on brokers + topics
missing_capabilities.description: Never sent. Anonymous DescribeConfigs on a broker leaks listener config, ssl.keystore.location, sasl.jaas.config paths, log.dirs, super.users, advertised.listeners for all listeners (including internal ones not returned by Metadata). On topics it leaks retention, cleanup.policy, min.insync.replicas — plus per-topic ACL policy. Massive info-disclosure primitive not attempted.

missing_capabilities.name: DescribeAcls (ApiKey=29)
missing_capabilities.description: Never sent. When anonymous access is allowed at all, DescribeAcls typically works too and dumps the entire ACL table — every principal name (User:CN=..., User:alice), every resource, every permission — which is a complete authorization map of the cluster. Enumerates users for downstream spray.

missing_capabilities.name: Produce (ApiKey=0) write-test
missing_capabilities.description: No probe attempts a zero-byte Produce to a synthetic topic to prove ANONYMOUS write, which would elevate the finding to log-tampering / event-injection (poisoning audit sinks, forging billing events). A single acks=0 Produce is idempotent-safe on a fabricated topic name.

missing_capabilities.name: CreateTopics (ApiKey=19) permission test
missing_capabilities.description: Optional companion to the Produce test: a `validate_only=true` CreateTopics tells you whether an anonymous principal has cluster-level CREATE without actually creating anything. Currently no capability check.
missing_capabilities.protocol_reference: Kafka protocol CreateTopicsRequest v0-v7 (validate_only flag added v1)

missing_capabilities.name: ApiVersions response parsing for broker fingerprint
missing_capabilities.description: The ApiVersions response is read then discarded. Its (api_key, min, max) tuple set uniquely fingerprints the Kafka release line (e.g. presence of ApiKey 60 DescribeCluster => Kafka >= 2.8; max Produce=10 => >= 3.0; ApiKey 68 ConsumerGroupHeartbeat => >= 3.7 KIP-848). Without this, CVE mapping (CVE-2023-25194 Kafka Connect JNDI, CVE-2022-34917 mTLS auth bypass 3.0-3.2, CVE-2024-27309 replication ACL bypass) is impossible.

missing_capabilities.name: TLS wrapping for 9093 / 9094 listeners
missing_capabilities.description: is_kafka() lists 9093 (default SSL) and 9094 (common SASL_SSL) but probe() only ever opens a plain socket. On a TLS listener the plaintext ApiVersions is discarded and the probe currently mislabels the broker as `kafka_saslgated` when it may actually be an open unauthenticated SSL listener. Missing: ssl.wrap_socket handshake, client-cert-required detection (SSL alert 40 handshake_failure without cert vs successful handshake), and cert CN/SAN extraction.

missing_capabilities.name: mTLS client-auth detection
missing_capabilities.description: Even after TLS wrapping is added, distinguishing SSL-only from SSL-with-required-client-cert requires observing the CertificateRequest handshake message / alert 40. Currently no code path attempts this — an mTLS-gated broker is indistinguishable from a broken one.

missing_capabilities.name: DescribeCluster (ApiKey=60) — cluster_id + controller
missing_capabilities.description: Cluster_id and controller node are never emitted. Cluster_id correlates the same cluster across pivoted network paths (a broker discovered on a private subnet == the one seen on the perimeter). Not fetched.

missing_capabilities.name: DescribeUserScramCredentials (ApiKey=50)
missing_capabilities.description: When permitted for anonymous (rare but seen on misconfigured KRaft brokers), returns username + mechanism + iterations for every SCRAM user configured on the cluster. Full user enumeration for spray. Never attempted.

missing_capabilities.name: CreateDelegationToken (ApiKey=38)
missing_capabilities.description: With cluster-level auth (post-cred), issuing a delegation token yields a portable HMAC credential usable from any client without further creds. Currently no post-auth exploit primitive.

missing_capabilities.name: is_internal / __consumer_offsets classification
missing_capabilities.description: _parse_metadata_v1 reads the is_internal bool then skips it. Findings therefore treat `__consumer_offsets` and `__transaction_state` as equivalent to user topics, inflating the topic list shown to the operator and hiding the more interesting user topics behind Kafka housekeeping ones.

missing_capabilities.name: Compact / flexible-versions parser (v9+)
missing_capabilities.description: Parser is hardcoded to v1 wire format (int16-length strings, int32 array counts). Modern KRaft brokers (>= 2.4 for many APIs) support only flexible/compact framing (varint lengths, tagged fields). The module works today only because it requests v1 explicitly; it cannot follow the ApiVersions-advertised maximum and so cannot use any of the KIP-482 flexible-only APIs.

priority_gaps: SaslHandshake enumeration — one request per SASL-gated broker, tells the whole session which mechanism to spray. Blocks credentialed pivot until added.
SaslAuthenticate with creds — analyze() takes a creds arg and drops it on the floor. Every other credentialed service in recce is worth more if kafka feeds it a proven principal.
Fetch a bounded sample from leaked topics — the finding currently says `topic names disclose intent`; a real fetch upgrades it from inventory-leak to data-disclosure with proof bytes.
TLS wrapping for 9093/9094 — module already claims to probe those ports; today it lies about them, calling every SSL-only listener SASL-gated.
DescribeConfigs + DescribeAcls — the two highest-yield anonymous read primitives after Metadata; leaks JAAS paths, super.users, and full principal list.
ApiVersions response parsing — cheap (already read, just parse) and unlocks version-specific CVE mapping (CVE-2023-25194, CVE-2022-34917, CVE-2024-27309).
cross_service_wire_gaps: Advertised broker `host` values are parsed but never fed back into the recce hosts registry as newly-discovered targets. On perimeter-exposed brokers this routinely leaks internal FQDNs / RFC1918 IPs (advertised.listeners) that no other scanner would see — a free pivot list.
Broker `rack` field is parsed then dropped. Rack IDs commonly encode DC/AZ (`us-east-1a`, `dc2-rack7`) — topology facts other modules (bgp, snmp, cloud-metadata) could correlate.
controller_id is skipped. The controller node is the correct target for control-plane abuse (metadata mutation, ACL changes); no other service can name it.

Enumerated SASL mechanisms should be published to the credentials/spray module so `PLAIN` on kafka reuses looted LDAP passwords, `GSSAPI` triggers the Kerberos playbook, `OAUTHBEARER` marks a Keycloak/JWT dependency.

Consumer-group DescribeGroups member.client_host values are effectively a list of every downstream service host — cross-fed into recce hosts, these become new scan targets that would not otherwise be reachable from the scanner's vantage point.

Topic-name heuristics: presence of `_schemas` implies Confluent Schema Registry (8081) alongside; `connect-configs` / `connect-offsets` / `connect-status` implies Kafka Connect REST (8083) — recce has no cross-service handoff to schedule those probes when kafka observes those topic names.

DescribeConfigs (when added) will expose `sasl.jaas.config`, `ssl.truststore.location`, and inter-broker listener addresses — these are host and credential facts that belong in the shared session store, not in a single kafka finding.
notes: The module's docstring still says `MetadataRequest v0` in two places while the code actually sends v1 (probe() line 197, module header line 3). Not a capability gap so omitted from the ranked list, but worth noting for the next editor. Also: probe() always uses correlation_id=1 and never validates the response's correlation_id — a hostile listener could return canned bytes claiming to be a Kafka reply and the parser would accept it; low-severity robustness, not an attack primitive.
